title: “Overdependence on algorithms?”: how artificial intelligence ethical leadership can safeguard self-efficacy and spur innovation
abstract: Abstract While the adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) is often heralded as a catalyst for cognitive augmentation, it simultaneously introduces a risk of cognitive offloading that may threaten human agency. Drawing on the human agency perspective of Social Cognitive Theory, this study investigates the paradoxical relationship between AI dependence and employee innovative behavior. We propose a moderated mediation model to explain how the dependence on “proxy agency” (AI dependence) has a reciprocal relationship with “personal agency” (self-efficacy) to influence innovation, and how AI ethical leadership functions as a contextual safeguard. We tested our hypotheses using data collected from 421 full-time employees in South Korea via a three-wave time-lagged research design. The results reveal a counterintuitive mechanism regarding the impact of AI. We found that AI dependence does not have a significant direct negative effect on innovative behavior. Instead, it inhibits innovation exclusively through a full mediation pathway by eroding employee self-efficacy. This indicates that the suppression of innovation is caused not by the technology itself, but by the “deprivation of mastery experiences” that accompanies over-dependence. Furthermore, we found that AI ethical leadership acts as a critical boundary condition. Under high levels of ethical leadership, the agency-eroding effect of AI dependence on self-efficacy was neutralized, thereby sustaining innovative behavior. These findings challenge technological determinism by highlighting the primacy of psychological resources and offer theoretical and practical insights for fostering a symbiotic human-AI relationship in the modern workplace.

title: mTOR signaling contributes to system-driven rhythmic gene expression in mouse liver
abstract: Rhythmic gene expression is essential to the daily organization of biological processes. While cycling transcriptomes are regulated by circadian clocks present in nearly every cell, accumulating evidence indicates that they can also be initiated by rhythmic food-driven systemic signals independently of circadian clocks. The underlying mechanisms remain however largely unknown. Here, we show that signaling through the nutrient-sensing kinase mechanistic target of rapamycin (mTOR) is both necessary and sufficient to mediate food-driven hepatic rhythmic gene expression, rhythmic regulation of the liver metabolome, and endoplasmic reticulum stress response. Acute inhibition of mTOR before the active phase desynchronizes the phase of mTOR-driven rhythmic genes without affecting clock-controlled rhythmic genes, indicating that alignment of rhythmic mTOR activity to the circadian cycle is critical for overt cycling transcriptomes. These findings may explain how misalignment between clock and systemic signals contributes to disease and underscore the use of mTOR inhibitors for resynchronizing system-driven rhythms and alleviating circadian rhythm disorders.

title: When resistance becomes knowledge: governing health-care AI through federated learning and explainable AI
journal: VINE Journal of Information and Knowledge Management Systems
abstract: Purpose Digital transformation in health care is frequently delayed by resistance, which is typically conceptualized as a barrier to AI adoption. This study aims to reframe resistance as a knowledge-generating signal, examining how it shapes organizational learning and knowledge governance during AI implementation in high-stakes, regulated settings. Design/methodology/approach The study draws on a canonical action research program conducted within the eHealth Network: Artificial Intelligence and Innovative ICT Tools Oriented toward Digital Diagnostics project. Empirical material was collected across nephrology, hepatology and diabetology through 55 interdisciplinary meetings, 17 semistructured interviews and extensive project documentation, enabling longitudinal analysis of how knowledge is produced, negotiated and institutionalized during AI implementation. Findings The findings show that resistance operates as diagnostic signal, revealing misalignments across conceptual, representational and evidential knowledge proximities. These tensions trigger the development of boundary infrastructures, including shared vocabularies, standardized test datasets and interdisciplinary routines, through which knowledge is created, validated and governed across professional communities. The analysis identifies two socio-technical mechanisms that mediate these knowledge tensions: federated learning, which functions as a knowledge-governance capability balancing data sovereignty with institutional learning and explainable AI, which, when institutionalized through clinical explanation rounds, supports collective sensemaking and embeds interpretability into everyday decision-making routines. Originality/value The study contributes to the knowledge management and information systems literature by reconceptualizing resistance as a generative constraint for governing knowledge in AI-enabled organizations. It advances understanding of how socio-technical mechanisms can transform resistance into an asset for organizational learning under epistemic pluralism, offering insights applicable beyond health care to other regulated and knowledge-intensive domains.

title: Welfare impacts of non-timber forest product exploitation: evidence from rural households in Burkina Faso
abstract: This paper examines the relationship between non-timber forest product (NTFP) exploitation and the welfare of rural households in Burkina Faso. Using survey data collected from 528 rural households, this study uses an endogenous switching regression (ESR) model complemented by propensity score matching (PSM) as a robustness analysis. Household welfare is measured using two key indicators, namely, per capita income and per capita food expenditures. The empirical findings suggest that participation in NTFP exploitation is positively associated with household welfare outcomes. ESR estimates indicate that households engaged in NTFP exploitation would have experienced an average reduction of approximately €190.25 per capita in income and €144.24 per capita in food expenditures had they not participated in these activities. Conversely, nonparticipating households could potentially achieve gains of about €36.54 per capita in income and €74.79 per capita in food expenditures through participation in NTFP exploitation. Although the estimated treatment effects differ somewhat across econometric approaches, the PSM results remain qualitatively consistent with the ESR findings, supporting the robustness of the positive association between NTFP exploitation and household welfare. Overall, the results suggest that NTFP exploitation constitutes an important livelihood strategy for improving income and food security among rural households. However, the sustainability of these welfare gains may be threatened by the degradation of forest resources resulting from climate change and increasing exploitation pressure. The study therefore highlights the need to strengthen sustainable forest management policies, social protection mechanisms and alternative income diversification strategies in rural areas.

title: Viewpoint – recruiting talent in the age of AI: essential human skills and effective hiring practices
abstract: Purpose This study aims to identify the human competencies that artificial intelligence (AI) tools cannot replicate effectively. It proposes strategies for hiring managers to identify and assess such skills. It also provides a practical framework for business leaders to develop a skilled workforce in AI-augmented organizations. Design/methodology/approach This viewpoint builds on existing literature on human resource management in AI-enabled workplaces. The views are based on the author’s extensive hiring experience as a general manager/product management executive in the consumer electronics domain and recruitment interactions with 100 + candidates for over 20 roles. Structured conversations with 16 cross-functional executives across product management, marketing, engineering and HR were also leveraged for empirical insights. Findings Five areas of human skills consistently emerge as essential in the AI-enabled business landscape: intuition and experiential wisdom, critical thinking, storytelling, ethical governance and relationship intelligence. Conventional hiring processes are insufficient for identifying such talent. Redesigning job architecture and using realistic business case studies significantly improve hiring efficiency in AI-enabled organizations. Research limitations/implications The findings primarily reflect large enterprise context and North American business environment. Future research should explore applications in smaller organizations and other geographies. Empirical and practitioner observations refer to the consumer electronics manufacturing domain. AI requirements can vary across business sectors. Practical implications HR leaders and hiring managers should collaborate to rebuild job architectures and hiring practices to focus on essential human competencies that cannot be effectively replicated by AI tools. Interview protocols should be retooled to examine realistic business applications and interpersonal narration skills. Organizations should strategically integrate AI into business processes without diminishing the value of critical thinking, narration and relationship-building capabilities. Originality/value Literature on practitioner-centric and empirically informed frameworks for efficiently identifying essential human competencies is limited. This paper summarizes effective hiring strategies in the age of AI and executive insights validated through business experience. Practical solutions are provided to continuously adopt AI in business processes.

title: Treatment of Typical and Atypical Trigeminal Neuralgia with LINAC-Based Radiosurgery: Complications, Recurrence Rates and Long-Term Treatment Outcomes
abstract: Background/Objectives: Linear accelerator (LINAC)-based radiosurgery (SRS) is a well-established, non-invasive treatment for pharmacologically refractory trigeminal neuralgia. Despite its widespread use, long-term efficacy and recurrence rates remain incompletely defined, highlighting the need for extended follow-up studies to assess outcome durability. Methods: All patients diagnosed with trigeminal neuralgia and treated with LINAC-based SRS (60 Gy, 1–2 mm from the nerve root entry zone) between 2012 and 2019 at a single institution, a national reference center, were recruited for this study. Patients were divided into two categories based on the nature of their neuralgia: typical or atypical. Pain control was assessed using the Barrow Neurological Institute (BNI) scale at 12, 36 and 60 months, as well as time to improvement, recurrence, and adverse effects. Results: A total of 112 patients were analyzed, with a mean follow-up period of 105.14 (SD 30.65) months. Statistically significant differences in the success of pain control (BNI I–III) between patients with typical and atypical neuralgia were observed at all evaluated time points (12 months: 87.1% vs. 44.0%, 36 months: 77.0% vs. 22.0%, and 60 months: 60.7% vs. 18.0%) (p < 0.001). The mean time to improvement was 6.32 (SD 6.61) weeks (range 0–50), and the recurrence rate following initial improvement was 47.1%. Treatment-related adverse clinical events occurred in 5.4% of patients. Conclusions: Long-term pain control is achieved in refractory trigeminal neuralgia cases with LINAC-based SRS, especially in typical cases, with a low incidence of complications.

title: Restoration of degraded cropland in the Pearl River Delta, China, through integrated agronomic measures: a modeling approach
abstract: Introduction Guangdong Province is an important grain and agricultural product production area in China, but part of the cultivated land in the Pearl River Delta has long been faced with complex degradation problems such as soil acidification, heavy metal pollution and lack of available phosphorus. These factors have posed continuous pressure on the sustainable development of regional agriculture and the restoration of farmland ecological functions. Methods Based on the multi-source data of 10 typical degraded farmland samples in the Pearl River Delta, this study constructed an analysis framework combining random forest and response surface method. Firstly, the random forest model was used to identify the key variables closely related to the soil function restoration index; Then box - Behnken design and response surface methodology were used to evaluate the comprehensive effects of biochar dosage, lime dosage and legume crop configuration on soil physical and chemical properties, CD bioavailability and microbial diversity. Results The results showed that available phosphorus and pH were the two variables most closely related to soil functional recovery index. Compared with the traditional remediation treatment, the biochar lime combined treatment was related to the increase of soil porosity, soil organic carbon and the proportion of residual CD, indicating that it had better comprehensive performance in improving soil environmental conditions and promoting CD stabilization. Among the tested legume crops, Astragalus sinicus is relatively superior in nitrogen fixation ability, microbial diversity, available phosphorus improvement, soil organic carbon increase and CD bioavailability reduction. In general, the combination of biochar 8 T/ha, lime 3 T/HA and Astragalus sinicus achieved a relatively balanced result among soil function recovery index, CD bioavailability control and input cost. Discussion This study combined random forest key factor identification, response surface parameter optimization and field validation, and provided a more specific decision-making basis for the zoning restoration of acidified degraded farmland and the selection of comprehensive agronomic measures in the Pearl River Delta. The results are helpful to optimize the restoration scheme of degraded farmland from the perspective of comprehensive trade-off among soil function restoration, heavy metal stabilization and cost constraint.

title: When leadership feels attainable: organizational cues shape black employees’ leadership aspirations
journal: International Journal of Contemporary Hospitality Management
abstract: Purpose Developing a sustainable managerial pipeline for black hospitality employees is crucial to establishing a more inclusive, equitable environment. This study aims to identify and assess barriers and facilitators that influence leadership self-efficacy, retention and intent to apply for leadership roles. Design/methodology/approach This study used an exploratory sequential mixed-methods design with black hourly hospitality employees. Study 1 (n = 20) conducted online structured interviews to identify barriers and facilitators to leadership. Partial least squares - structural equation modeling was used in Study 2 (n = 145) to test the effects of identified facilitators, and in Study 3 (n = 167) to test the effects of identified barriers on pipeline outcomes. Findings Seven themes emerged from the interviews. Quantitative results showed mentorship (theme 1), Employee resource groups (theme 2a), inclusive culture (theme 2 b), development (theme 3), help-seeking (theme 4a) and self-leadership (theme 4 b) improved leadership intent, retention and leadership self-efficacy. Customer-oriented racism (theme 5a), organizational-oriented racism (theme 5 b), evaluation bias (theme 6), generational conflict (theme 7a), ignorance excuse (theme 7 b) and stereotyping (theme 7c) negatively impacted all three outcomes. Research limitations/implications By identifying barriers and facilitators to leadership, the study illustrates why black employees remain underrepresented. Systemic issues, not employee aspirations, are the primary issue for the chronic underrepresentation. Originality/value This study takes an unconventional, bottom-up approach to examining the underrepresentation of black employees in leadership. Attribution theory is extended to include organizational attributes that lead to perceptions of success and failure.
